own_inferences: The question hinges on reliably identifying PNR failures and PULL_UP actions from play‑by‑play, and on having sufficient observations per defensive unit to estimate a lift of at least 2 points per possession. Given the granularity of the data and the rarity of both PNR failures and PULL_UP events in many units, the analysis will likely suffer from exposure sparsity and low statistical power. Additionally, the definition of a “unit” (team, defensive matchup, or set) is ambiguous, which further complicates the estimation of a consistent lift across units.
uncertainties: Exact operationalization of PNR fail and PULL_UP; the granularity of the units; the frequency of the events; potential confounding by offensive strength or matchup quality.

historical_effect.explanation: No prior studies were found that addressed this specific hypothesis, so the decision is based solely on theoretical assessment of feasibility.

blocking_constraints.text: PNR failures and PULL_UP events are relatively rare, limiting observations per unit.
Identifying PNR failures and PULL_UP actions from play‑by‑play may be error‑prone.
Units that experience PNR failures may differ systematically in offensive/defensive quality.
Many units will have too few observations to estimate a 2‑point lift with confidence.

prior_work.summary: No relevant prior work was retrieved.

risks.text: Low frequency of the key events limits power.
Potential misclassification of PNR failures and PULL_UP actions.
Unmeasured differences between units may bias lift estimates.
Insufficient sample size per unit for detecting a 2‑pp lift.

design.estimand: Average lift in points per possession attributable to PULL_UP following a PNR failure, measured across defensive units.
design.sample: All units with at least 30 possessions involving PNR failure and PULL_UP events across seasons 2022‑23 to 2025‑26
design.power: Not achievable given exposure sparsity and unit-level data constraints
design.controls: Offensive rating, defensive rating, opponent strength, game context variables
design.falsification: Compare lift on units with PNR success to check for systematic bias
design.multiplicity: None, single hypothesis test per unit aggregated across units
design.decision_rule: Reject if <70% of units show lift>0 or median lift<2pp
design.data_version: NBA 2022‑23 to 2025‑26 per‑game play‑by‑play and derived possession records

You work only from the task statement and the tools listed below. Do not assume facts you have not seen.

The work has two stages, in this order.

2. Identify the research concepts and methodological questions the task raises.

The stage-2 output format is given together with the retrieval result.

no tool returned. In some settings retrieval returns no records; then state that no historical evidence was available.

Protocol: every reply is exactly one JSON object and nothing else.
To call a tool: {"action": "tool", "tool": "<name>", "args": {...}}
To finish (stage 2 only): {"action": "final", "output": <object following the stage-2 schema>}
You may call at most 12 tools; then you must finish. Check that every opening brace has a closing brace.
